K2/K3 coils, the VMOT eFuse enable (RUN_HD) and the nSLEEP gate input are all fed through K1 pole B and U_HOLD from CHAIN_END. They lose their supply as soon as the opened element interrupts CHAIN_END; neither the brake relays nor VMOT removal wait for K1 to release (K1 release only matters for the latch). The K2/K3 coil current additionally loses its return through U_LS. "No restart without REARM" rests on K1 AND U_HOLD (stage 3).

### T5. Slope and holding

Dynamic braking produces force only while moving: braking coefficient 343 N per m/s (conservative) / 624 (nominal). It cannot hold a slope. Gearbox friction (12.7 N [A]) holds the stationary robot up to about 6.2 deg (3.1 deg with half the friction); beyond that the unpowered robot creeps at (m g sin(theta) - F_fric) / c, e.g. 41 mm/s on a 10 deg ramp with half friction. A parking brake is not fitted; the operating envelope must exclude slopes above the measured holding angle (VT open).

### T6. Brake resistor and contact stress

- v0 = 0.20 m/s: kinetic energy 0.91 J (high inertia), peak brake current 1.97 A, peak resistor power 3.9 W, energy per resistor <= 0.14 J. [C]
- v0 = 0.44 m/s (runaway at 14.4 V no-load speed): kinetic energy 4.34 J (high inertia), peak brake current 4.31 A, peak resistor power 18.6 W, energy per resistor <= 0.67 J. [C]
- Relay contacts (G2RL-2: 8 A, 30 V DC resistive [D family]) break at most the bridge current limit 2.68 A and make at most the brake current above. [C]

### T7. Regeneration and bus clamp

- Largest energy the drive can return in a controlled stop from 0.20 m/s: 0.91 J (all kinetic energy, no losses) [C]. Peak regenerated power if both bridges brake at the current limit: 2 x 2.68 A x 6.3 V = 34 W for a few tens of ms [C].
- Bus capacitance 1010 uF (VMOT 3 x 270 uF + VBAT_SW): absorbing 0.91 J alone would lift 14.4 V to 44.7 V [C] - so a clamp is required when nothing else takes the energy (BMS open).
- Clamp: comparator on VMOT, on at 15.6 V, off at 15.0 V [design], two 9.1 ohm 2512 pulse-rated resistors in parallel (R149/R150 class, 4.55 ohm) behind the 1.1 A PTC F_CLAMP -> 3.4 A, 53 W peak at 15.6 V (> 34 W regenerated). Pulse energy <= 0.9 J per stop. [C]
- With the pack connected and accepting charge the standing load (>= 15 W) is usually larger than the average regenerated power and the bus does not rise; the clamp is for the BMS-open and full-pack cases. [C]
- Stuck-on clamp: 13 V / 4.55 ohm = 2.9 A, 37 W continuous in a 4 W resistor pair -> a 1.1 A-hold PTC in series trips in a few seconds [A]; BUS_CLAMP_ACTIVE readback and the INA228 offset make it visible. [C]

### T8. Braking on a slope (downhill, braked, conservative constant, 12 kg)

m_eff dv/dt = m g sin(theta) - F_fric - c v. If m g sin(theta) < F_fric the robot stops; otherwise it never stops and creeps at v_inf = (m g sin(theta) - F_fric) / c. Distance from 0.20 m/s includes the 10.8 ms contact-element delay; *creep* = distance in the first 2 s after the event. F_fric = 16.2 N nominal (rolling + gearboxes [A]) or half; rolling resistance is included because the robot is moving (T5's static holding angle uses the gearbox friction alone). [C]

| Slope | Friction | m g sin(theta) (N) | Stops? | Distance from 0.20 m/s (mm) | Creep speed (mm/s) | Distance in 2 s (mm) |
|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 deg | nominal | 0.0 | yes | 18 | 0 | 18 |
| 0 deg | half | 0.0 | yes | 22 | 0 | 22 |
| 3 deg | nominal | 6.2 | yes | 21 | 0 | 21 |
| 3 deg | half | 6.2 | yes | 26 | 0 | 26 |
| 6 deg | nominal | 12.3 | yes | 24 | 0 | 24 |
| 6 deg | half | 12.3 | **no** | never stops | 12 | 52 |
| 10 deg | nominal | 20.4 | **no** | never stops | 12 | 52 |
| 10 deg | half | 20.4 | **no** | never stops | 36 | 96 |

The braked robot holds a downhill slope only through gearbox and rolling friction (assumed, not measured). Trailer door ramps above about 3 deg (half friction) are outside what the chain can hold; the operating envelope must exclude them until the holding angle is measured (o3).

### T9. Hot windings (stopping distance from 0.20 m/s, contact element, level floor)

Winding resistance rises 0.393 %/K [D copper]; R_M = 2.18 ohm is the cold (20 C) extrapolated stall value. Magnet flux of a ferrite motor falls about 0.2 %/K [A] (KE and the force constant together), which reduces the braking coefficient with the square. [C]

| Winding temperature | R_M (ohm) | Brake loop (ohm) | Flux factor | Braking coeff. cons. (N per m/s) | Total nominal (mm) | Total conservative (mm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 20 C | 2.18 | 3.22 | 1.00 | 343 | 8.8 | 28.6 |
| 60 C | 2.52 | 3.56 | 1.00 | 310 | 9.3 | 31.4 |
| 100 C | 2.87 | 3.91 | 1.00 | 283 | 9.8 | 34.2 |
| 100 C + magnet | 2.87 | 3.91 | 0.84 | 200 | 12.0 | 47.5 |

A hot winding (100 C) lengthens the conservative distance by about a quarter; with the magnet derating about two thirds. These are calculated, not measured; the spin-down test (first power-up step 12) should be repeated warm.

### T11. K1 set from the reservoir at the SET_READY threshold (stage 4, follow-up review N1)

SET_READY (U33B) rises at C_SET = 10.77 V (10.57-10.99 V with 1 % resistors and the 0.5 % LM4040C) and falls at 9.32 V [C]. A press while SET_READY is low does not reach U_SET (Q_SETC in the stack), so the reservoir is never dumped by an early press. At the moment SET_READY is first high C_SET holds at least 10.57 V; the table gives the time the K1 coil current stays above the must-operate current 8.75 mA (9 V / 1028 ohm, 75 % of rated at 23 C [D family G6S, U]; ampere-turns, so the same current at any coil temperature) with C_SET -20 % / nominal, D_RSET not in the discharge path, U_SET 0.15 ohm. Guaranteed set = >= 6 ms (1.5 x the 4 ms operate time [U]). The coil is at board temperature at K1 (RT1, moved next to K1 in stage 5) plus its own self-heating after an armed period (0.17 W, up to about +10 K [A], firmware H2). [C]

| Coil (board) temperature | Coil R (ohm) | Must-operate voltage (V) | Time above must-operate, C_SET 80 uF (ms) | Same, 100 uF (ms) | Set at SET_READY? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| -25 C | 834 | 7.30 | 24.7 | 30.9 | yes |
| +0 C | 935 | 8.18 | 19.1 | 23.9 | yes |
| +23 C | 1028 | 9.00 | 13.3 | 16.6 | yes |
| +35 C | 1076 | 9.42 | 9.9 | 12.4 | yes |
| +45 C | 1117 | 9.77 | 7.0 | 8.7 | yes |
| +50 C | 1137 | 9.95 | 5.5 | 6.9 | marginal |
| +60 C | 1177 | 10.30 | 2.4 | 3.0 | marginal |
| +85 C | 1278 | 11.19 | 0.0 | 0.0 | **no**: REARM_REFUSED COIL_HOT |

Design limit: a set at the SET_READY threshold is guaranteed up to a **+45 C** board (coil) temperature; above it firmware reports COIL_HOT (a press may still set when C_SET has charged above the threshold). The limit is an assumption on the trailer environment [A]; raising it needs a higher threshold and so a higher minimum supply.

### T12. Time from chain closure to SET_READY, and the minimum supply to arm (stage 4, N1)

C_SET charges from CHAIN_END through D_RSET (0.4 V [A]) and R_SET 15 k; the 1.357 M divider limits the final voltage to 0.989 x (CHAIN_END - 0.4 V); tau 1.48 s (C_SET +/-20 %: 1.19-1.78 s). CHAIN_END is the pack voltage less F_CHAIN and the photo-MOS drops (< 0.1 V before latching) [C].

| Pack (V) | Final C_SET (V) | To SET_READY, nominal (s) | Worst (C +20 %, threshold high) (s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 11.0 | 10.38 | never | never |
| 11.2 | 10.58 | never | never |
| 11.4 | 10.78 | 11.3 | never |
| 11.6 | 10.98 | 5.9 | never |
| 12.0 | 11.37 | 4.4 | 6.0 |
| 12.8 | 12.16 | 3.2 | 4.2 |
| 13.3 | 12.66 | 2.8 | 3.6 |
| 14.4 | 13.75 | 2.3 | 2.9 |

**Minimum supply at which the robot can be armed: 11.7 V** (worst-case threshold; 11.4 V nominal). Below it SET_READY never comes and the firmware reports REARM_NOT_READY / SUPPLY_LOW; the firmware's own BATTERY_LOW stop is 11.2 V. A legitimate press with SET_READY high does not wait for anything else. Every interruption of CHAIN_END longer than 41-64 ms empties C_SET again (Q_SDIS, tau 0.1 s), shorter dips do not (C_SDB on the discharge gate). [C]

### T13. REARM qualification and pulse timing (stage 4, N2)

Set contact closes at t = 0 and stays closed (REARM_SET_RAW = 4.65-4.9 V from V5_AUX via 1 k / 47 k). Q_SETA conducts while SET_G exceeds its threshold (BSS138 0.8-1.5 V [D]). C_SF 2.2 uF and C_SC 1 uF X7R at +/-20 % (DC-bias derating at 5 V included in the -20 % corner [A]). Release of the set contact ends the pulse at once (D_SGN) [C, numerical].

| Corner | Pulse can start after (ms) | Pulse length if held (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| earliest (C -20 %, 4.9 V, Vth 0.8 V) | 3.2 | 166 |
| nominal (Vth 1.1 V) | 6.0 | 168 |
| latest (C +20 %, 4.65 V, Vth 1.5 V) | 11.2 | 151 |
| shortest pulse (C -20 %, 4.65 V, Vth 1.5 V) | 7.4 | 101 |

Firmware guarantee: no set pulse can start before the set contact has been closed for the 'earliest' time above; both REARM contacts are sampled at 1 kHz on IOX_A (GPB2, GPB6), so every press that can set the latch is seen in at least 3 samples. A press released after the start but before K1 (<= 4 ms [U]) and U_HOLD (<= 3 ms [U]) have both closed can leave K1 sealed with RUN_HD dead: firmware treats it as REARM_REFUSED (PARTIAL), non-fatal, and drops ARM_PERMIT for 30 ms (firmware as of 2026-11-28, ICD section 4.6; short enough to keep C_SET, since the discharge cannot start before 41 ms: H4). Q_SETC gate (100 k / 470 nF): on 13-28 ms after SET_READY rises, off 37-67 ms after it falls (the falling hysteresis adds about 15 ms of dump before that). C_SET discharge gate (100 k || 56 k, 1 uF): discharge starts 41-64 ms after CHAIN_END dies, stops 6-13 ms after it returns. [C]

### T14. Leakage into photo-MOS LEDs (stage 4, follow-up review N5)

An element is held only if its LED gets a meaningful forward current. TLP241A: IFT (guaranteed on) <= 3 mA [U]; the current at which the output starts to conduct is not specified: **0.1 mA is assumed as the lowest current that may hold an element partly on** [A]. Leakage values are recalled family values [U] at the maximum reverse / off voltage; board temperature +60 C / +85 C. [C]

| Element | Leakage path into the LED node | Leakage +60 C / +85 C | Shunt across the LED path | LED current (+85 C) | vs 0.1 mA |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| U_LS, U_HOLD (RUN_HD) - stage 3 | D_RUN B160 Schottky, RUN_12V held up, 14.6 V reverse | 1-3 mA / 3-10 mA | LEDs 1.5 k each, dividers >= 122 k | up to several mA | **fails** (N5) |
| U_LS, U_HOLD (RUN_HD) - stage 4 | D_RUN S1G silicon, 14.6 V reverse | 2-5 uA / 5-20 uA | R_RHD 10 k to GND: RUN_HD <= 0.2 V (< LED Vf) | ~0 | ok |
| U_LS, U_HOLD (RUN_HD) | U_HOLD off-state, K1_RUN live (K1 welded) | <= 1 uA / <= 10 uA [U] | R_RHD 10 k | ~0 | ok |
| U_HOLD (HOLD_A) | Q_HSET BSS84 off, 5 V across | <= 1 uA / <= 10 uA [U] | R_HA 1.5 k + R_RHD 10 k to GND (0.12 V) | ~0 | ok |
| U_SET | 4-FET stack off (BSS138), 3.7 V | <= 0.5 uA / <= 5 uA [U] | none needed (series) | <= 5 uA | ok |
| U21, U21B, U22, U23, U24, U20 | driver BSS138 off (Q22, Q_LB, Q28, Q23, Q24, Q20) | <= 0.5 uA / <= 5 uA [U] | series | <= 5 uA | ok |
| loop channels A/B inputs | loop self-test FETs Q_LTA/Q_LTB off-state into LOOP_F / LOOP_FB | <= 0.5 uA / <= 5 uA [U] | R69 / R_LB1 10 k | (not an LED) -50 mV on a 1.56 V signal, towards 'open' | ok |

The K2/K3 coil-hold case of the review (G2RL must-release about 5 % of rated [U]) cannot arise in stage 4: U_LS cannot be held by leakage, so the coil return opens. [C]

Pads SVC1-SVC10 (TP63-TP72, top side, 2 x 5 at 2.54 mm): SVC1 GND; SVC2 CHAIN_END, SVC3 K1_RUN, SVC4 RUN_HD, SVC5 RUN_12V, SVC6 RELAY_RTN, SVC7 HOLD_A, SVC8 LS_A, SVC9 CH_N6A, SVC10 SET_CAP, each behind 220 k 1 %. Pin-short safety: any pad to 14.6 V drives <= 66 uA into its node (any two pads: <= 33 uA). Worst cases: K1 coil 834 ohm at -25 C sees <= 55 mV (must-release 0.97 V at -25 C); RUN_HD (10 k bleed) <= 0.66 V, below a photo-MOS LED's forward voltage, and 0.66 V x 22/122 = 0.12 V on U8 EN (1.2 V threshold); RUN_12V into the coils <= 12 mV; RELAY_RTN to GND through 220 k carries <= 66 uA of coil current (release current several mA); HOLD_A / LS_A <= 66 uA LED current (< the 0.1 mA assumed holding level, T14); CH_N6A / CHAIN_END lifted to <= 6.2 V through the 156 k taps (no coil fed: K1 needs 1.16 mA to hold; the firmware may report CHAIN_IMPLAUSIBLE, fail-safe); SET_CAP: C_SET is held at 0 by Q_SDIS while the chain is open, and charging it while closed is the normal state. Pad to GND: removes at most 66 uA from a node. [C]
